cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is still writing to the church in Corinth about tongues and prophecy. Now he asks, "What then shall we say, brothers?" When they come together, everyone brings something: a psalm, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue or an interpretation.

cards.question: When the Corinthian church comes together, everybody brings a psalm, a teaching, a tongue or something else. What does Paul say all of it must do?

cards.text: First up: speaking in tongues, and Paul puts a NUMBER on it. Good, because the whole room going at once isn't a meeting, friend, it's a group chat with ninety-nine unread messages.

cards.question: In a meeting, ___ or at most ___ people should speak in a tongue, taking turns.
The people speaking in a tongue in Corinth take turns. What else does Paul say must happen?

cards.text: But what if nobody in the room can interpret? Paul's got a plan for that too.

cards.question: True or false: in Corinth, when there's no interpreter, Paul says the one with a tongue should speak up anyway.

cards.text: With no interpreter, he stays silent in the church and speaks only to himself and God. Next come the prophets, and two or three of them should speak.

cards.question: Two or three prophets speak in the Corinthian meeting. What should everyone else do?

cards.text: Now picture a prophet mid-message, and suddenly someone sitting down gets a revelation. This is the work meeting where two people start talking at once and then do the "no, YOU go" dance for ten straight minutes.

cards.question: A prophet in Corinth is speaking, and a revelation comes to someone seated. What does Paul say should happen?

cards.text: Then Paul says they can ALL prophesy, one at a time. Same as my oven, friend: every batch gets in, just not all at once.

cards.question: Prophesying in turn means everyone in the Corinthian church can be instructed and ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets." I take that to mean a prophet can hold it and wait his turn, which is more than I can say for me standing next to a tray of warm cookies.

cards.question: Paul gives the reason for all these turns: God is not a God of ___, but of peace.
True or false: Paul says this way of peace is something only the church in Corinth has.

cards.text: Next, Paul writes, "Women are to be silent in the churches." He says they are not permitted to speak but must be in submission, as the law says, and if they want to ask about something, they should ask their own husbands at home.
Then Paul asks Corinth two questions: "Did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?" Whew, friend, Paul is NOT whispering.

cards.question: Paul says anyone in Corinth who thinks he's a prophet or spiritual should acknowledge something about what Paul is writing. What?

answers.text: It is just for this year

cards.question: If anyone ignores what Paul writes to Corinth, he himself will be ___.

cards.text: Now Paul wraps up everything he's said about tongues and prophecy with "So, my brothers." That's the oven timer going DING, friend, and it's time to pull the batch out.

cards.question: True or false: in his wrap-up, Paul tells the Corinthians to forbid speaking in tongues.
Paul tells his brothers in Corinth to be eager for one gift in particular. What is it?
Paul's last word to Corinth: everything must be done in a proper and ___ manner.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 5 quotes "So, my brothers.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The choice cards in stop 2 repeat a fixed cycle of types: multiple choice (card 3), fill in the blank (card 4), true or false (card 6), then multiple choice (card 7) and fill in the blank (card 8) again.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This story card has more than two beats. It covers four things: women are to be silent, they are not permitted to speak, they must be in submission as the law says, and they should ask their husbands at home. It should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The card cites 1 Corinthians 14:35 but leaves out the reason that verse gives ("for it is dishonorable for a woman to speak in the church"). No other card tells it, so the baker misses a stated detail of the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
